Specification: A specification of the Slush protocol, a probabilistic consensus algorithm in the Avalanche family. Each node loops a fixed number of iterations querying a sample set of other nodes and flipping its color choice when a threshold of replies disagree. The spec is a PlusCal model translated to TLA+; while TLA+ cannot reason about probabilities directly, the model serves as executable pseudocode and checks the termination property via TLC.
AssumptionNames: /\ Cardinality(Node) = Cardinality(SlushLoopProcess) /\ Cardinality(Node) = Cardinality(SlushQueryProcess) /\ SlushIterationCount \in Nat /\ SampleSetSize \in Nat /\ PickFlipThreshold \in Nat
IfThenElse: IF ~Terminate THEN /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "WaitForQueryMessageOrTermination"] ELSE /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "Done"]
IF Terminate THEN /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "QueryReplyLoop"] ELSE /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "RespondToQueryMessage"]
IF Pick(self) = NoColor THEN msg.color ELSE Pick(self)
IF loopVariant[self] < SlushIterationCount THEN /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "QuerySampleSet"] ELSE /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT ![self] = "SlushLoopTermination"]

IF redTally >= PickFlipThreshold THEN /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![HostOf[self]] = Red] ELSE /\ IF blueTally >= PickFlipThreshold THEN /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![HostOf[self]] = Blue] ELSE /\ TRUE /\ pick' = pick
IF blueTally >= PickFlipThreshold THEN /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![HostOf[self]] = Blue] ELSE /\ TRUE /\ pick' = pick
IF \E n \in Node : pick[n] = NoColor THEN /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT !["ClientRequest"] = "AssignColorToNode"] ELSE /\ pc' = [pc EXCEPT !["ClientRequest"] = "Done"]
IF pick[node] = NoColor THEN /\ pick' = [pick EXCEPT ![node] = color] ELSE /\ TRUE /\ pick' = pick
CaseExpr: CASE self \in SlushQueryProcess -> "QueryReplyLoop" [] self \in SlushLoopProcess -> "RequireColorAssignment" [] self = "ClientRequest" -> "ClientRequestLoop"
SetEnumeration: { m \in message : /\ m.type = QueryMessageType /\ m.dst = pid }
{ m \in message : /\ m.type = QueryReplyMessageType /\ m.dst = pid }
{[type |-> QueryReplyMessageType, src |-> self, dst |-> msg.src, color |-> color]}
{[type |-> QueryMessageType, src |-> self, dst |-> pid, color |-> Pick(self)] : pid \in sampleSet'[self]}
{msg \in message : /\ msg.type = QueryReplyMessageType /\ msg.src \in sampleSet[self] /\ msg.dst = self}
FunctionConstructor: [self \in ProcSet |-> CASE self \in SlushQueryProcess -> "QueryReplyLoop" [] self \in SlushLoopProcess -> "RequireColorAssignment" [] self = "ClientRequest" -> "ClientRequestLoop"]
RecordConstructor: [ type : {QueryMessageType}, src : SlushLoopProcess, dst : SlushQueryProcess, color : Color ]
[ type : {QueryReplyMessageType}, src : SlushQueryProcess, dst : SlushLoopProcess, color : Color ]
[type |-> QueryReplyMessageType, src |-> self, dst |-> msg.src, color |-> color]
[type |-> QueryMessageType, src |-> self, dst |-> pid, color |-> Pick(self)]
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE n \in Node : /\ \E mapping \in HostMapping : /\ n \in mapping /\ pid \in mapping
FunctionConstructor_ByDomain: [self \in ProcSet |-> CASE self \in SlushQueryProcess -> "QueryReplyLoop" [] self \in SlushLoopProcess -> "RequireColorAssignment" [] self = "ClientRequest" -> "ClientRequestLoop"]
DivisionNotes: TemporalNesting is false because the spec uses only the standard [][Next]_vars and a top-level <>(...) termination property without nesting temporal operators inside one another.

Action operators (QueryReplyLoop, WaitForQueryMessageOrTermination, RespondToQueryMessage, SlushQuery, RequireColorAssignment, ExecuteSlushLoop, QuerySampleSet, TallyQueryReplies, SlushLoopTermination, SlushLoop, ClientRequestLoop, AssignColorToNode, ClientRequest, Terminating, Next) appear in ActionDefNames because they contain primed variables or are disjunctions of such.

Set/value/helper definitions (HostOf, Red, Blue, Color, NoColor, the *MessageType strings, the message-record schemas, NoMessage, PendingQueryMessage, PendingQueryReplyMessage, Pick, vars, ProcSet) are placed in ValueDef as structural value definitions used by Init and the actions.
This spec contains a PlusCal algorithm 'Slush' with three processes (SlushQuery, SlushLoop, ClientRequest); these names are listed under PlusCalAlgorithm and PlusCalProcesses.
